prompt: Sodium and chlorine react to form sodium chloride. Using the outermost electrons of each atom, explain why the compound has the formula $\text{NaCl}$ rather than $\text{Na}_2\text{Cl}$.
teacher_notes: Expect valence electron counts and a charge-balance argument. Students who only say the atoms swap electrons have not addressed the ratio.
sample_solution: Sodium has one valence electron and loses it to reach a stable octet, forming $\text{Na}^+$. Chlorine has seven valence electrons and gains one to complete its octet, forming $\text{Cl}^-$. Because each sodium atom donates exactly one electron and each chlorine atom accepts exactly one, the ions must combine in a one-to-one ratio for the compound to be electrically neutral. $\text{Na}_2\text{Cl}$ would leave a net charge of $+1$, which is why that formula does not occur.
